title: Verification lab and field book
outcome: Turn one lesson into a reproducible evidence record another learner can check.
show: Fill a field-book sheet with a question, an input, a predicted result, an observation, and a source.
concepts: Open the Golden Goose mainnet verifier. Record the reported hash and observation time. Reproduce the header proof using the Mining Lab or an independent tool.
Bitcoin Core regtest creates a local development network where learners can produce practice blocks without joining Bitcoin mainnet. The practice chain uses its own local data.
Give a partner the public input and the source, plus the rule you used. Record whether they got the same result. Explain any difference before combining observations.
replicate: Pick the public verification route or the local practice route. Record which network you used.
Keep categories for observed, calculated, and claimed. Add a partner’s independent result with a timestamp.
check: What should a second learner need to reproduce the check?
The same public input or controlled local setup, the verification rule, the selected network, and the expected result format.

challenge.title: Reproduce a real header proof
challenge.prompt: Hash Bitcoin’s historical genesis header, change one byte, then check what happens to the proof.
challenge.tip: Hash the raw 80 bytes twice with SHA-256. Display the resulting bytes in reverse order and compare the integer to the header’s target.
